correctness.rationale: For each fixed labeled a–b path of s=k+1 vertices, classical rooted-forest determinant hN^(N−h−1) gives exactly s n^(n−s−1) tree extensions. For r prescribed off-path leaves and q prescribed path endpoints, removing these leaves gives (s−q)(n−r−q)^(n−s−1) extensions, so the joint inclusion probability is ((s−q)/s)((n−r−q)/n)^(n−s−1) (zero for q=s). Inclusion expansion yields the full conditional probability-generating polynomial, and singletons yield the stated mean. Exact subtraction gives signed factor 2(n−1)−k(k+1)^2 over a positive denominator, with a unique discrete sign transition, possible two-point plateau, and maximizing k∼(2n)^(1/3). At n=3 mean is 2 and at s=n the negative exponent cancels correctly. Separate independently written Prüfer enumeration tested 14 (n,k) conditional-mean cells for n=3..6; this finite check does not establish the unrestricted proof.
